analysis:
Examined all supplied workflow excerpts, documentation patches and file metadata. The complete workflow change map limits changes to selecting release toolchain mode (head 112–114) and requiring SDK 27.2 in the retained signed-artifact compatibility check (.github/workflows/release-provider.yml:1444). Neither change visibly weakens artifact identity or authorization. Surrounding checks retain hardened-runtime signing, entitlement verification, notarization, final archived signature checks, full CodeDirectory hashing, linked-SDK comparison (968–985), and artifact digest verification before older-OS execution (1438–1454). Publication remains separated from compilation and consumes retained signed artifacts; those surrounding mechanisms are unchanged, not new findings.
Changelog lines 3–7 and docs/developer/build.md:162–184 describe strict release SDK/Swift selection versus a broader qualification mode. Relevant contracts are A-011/A-017, T-013/T-034/T-054 and TB-011: toolchain validation must not be mistaken for independent build qualification or serving permission. No supplied change affects prompt encryption, key custody, cache isolation (T-041), billing, fan authority or local add-on controls.
Integration must verify scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh and scripts/provider-release-swift.sh actually enforce release SDK 27.2/Swift 6.4.2, propagate the selected Xcode to all build/signing tools, and that release preparation, signing validation and resumed unsigned builds consistently use the strict mode. These implementations/callers are outside this batch; documentation is not proof of enforcement. No concrete regression is established here, but toolchain enforcement remains a material cross-file review question.
